questions.question: List the documents and steps needed to open a savings account and explain why FICA requires them.
questions.expected_answer: Documents: ID/smart ID or birth certificate (minor) or passport; proof of residential address (municipal account, lease, letter); for a minor, the parent/guardian's ID and proof of address. Steps: choose a bank/account; gather documents; complete application (branch/online/app); make opening deposit; receive account number, card/app; set PIN. FICA requires verification of identity and address to prevent fraud, money laundering and crime.

questions.question: Explain how a rotating stokvel works, and calculate the payout for 8 members contributing R400 a month. Name two other community schemes.
questions.expected_answer: Members contribute a fixed amount regularly into a pool; each period the whole pool is paid to one member in turn until all have received it. Payout = 8 × R400 = R3 200 per month. Others: savings stokvel/club, grocery stokvel, investment stokvel, burial society.

questions.question: Give two advantages and two risks of community savings schemes, and two ways to reduce the risks.
questions.expected_answer: Advantages (any two): discipline; mutual support; lump sums without interest; bulk-buying discounts; access for people outside banking; help with funerals. Risks (any two): theft of cash; dishonest treasurer; members stop paying after payout; poor records and disputes; little legal protection; no interest on cash. Reduce (any two): written constitution; trustworthy office bearers and two signatures; records shared at meetings; keep money in a stokvel bank account; careful member selection.
